new_p0_p3_findings.title: Consume the actual one-record Git rename shape in native commit validation
new_p0_p3_findings.scenario: A native /commit selection includes both old.txt and new.txt for a staged rename. Actual GitTool status emits a single string ending new.txt plus tab-orig-old.txt, but check_staged_paths treats that whole suffix as the destination and expects a second array element for the origin. It rejects the selected rename as an unrelated staged path, preventing the commit.
evidence: git/tool.rs parse_status_records appends the origin to the rename record with record.push_str("\torig: ") and consumes the NUL origin field (2474-2485). Status output therefore has one JSON string per rename, explicitly documented by the producer.

check_staged_paths still splits type2 record into10 space-delimited parts, compares parts.last() directly to selected (slash/git.rs203-215), then advances the records iterator to obtain the origin (217-221). The destination is actually new.txt\torig: old.txt, so even selecting both real paths cannot satisfy this check.
Native commit executes this guard before staging and again immediately before commit (slash/git.rs639 and667). The model-facing Git commit operation itself does not have this mismatch.

Existing native guard tests fabricate [rename_record, old_filename] arrays, while producer tests explicitly assert one record ends with renamed.txt\torig: old. No existing test composes the real GitTool::Status result with its native consumer.
new_p0_p3_findings.fix: Align native validation with the actual bounded status result shape, preferably use structured destination/origin metadata shared with the producer. Preserve checking both source and destination and never consume the next unrelated record. Handle literal tabs/newlines or explicitly reject ambiguous spellings with a clear reason.
acceptance_tests: Run the supplied compositional fixture: actual GitTool status after git mv old.txt new.txt, both selected, must pass native staged-path validation. Reject when either rename path is outside selection. Include an unrelated staged record immediately after the rename and literal space/tab filename cases.
new_p0_p3_findings.validation: Source and indexed implementation confirmed; supplied compositional regression awaits root-coordinated Cargo.

p4_findings.title: Bound aggregate hook payloads after placeholder expansion
p4_findings.scenario: An otherwise accepted prompt hook repeats $ARGUMENTS throughout a source prompt below the32KiB setting cap. Each replacement copies a separately bounded64KiB event;2500 placeholders produce roughly156MiB before any provider request. MCP input templates below64KiB likewise repeat ${tool_response} and can multiply a normal bounded tool result into a very large JSON request.
evidence: settings.rs caps the authored model prompt at32KiB and authored MCP input JSON at64KiB; these checks run before expansion.

build_model_prompt sanitizes the event once to64KiB, then instructions.replace("$ARGUMENTS", &block) copies the block for every occurrence without an aggregate ceiling (backend.rs355-363). A25KiB source containing2500 markers remains admissible but allocates roughly164million output bytes.

substitute_event_values appends every resolved event string with push_str for every occurrence and recursively builds arrays/objects with no output budget (backend.rs158-200). run_mcp_tool sends that expanded object directly.
The outer asynchronous timeout cannot prevent the synchronous expansion allocation that occurs before the request future yields.
p4_findings.fix: Introduce an explicit aggregate post-expansion byte budget for model and MCP hook requests. Check capacity before appending/copying and return a static bounded hook failure when expansion would exceed it; do not silently truncate trusted instructions or alter the operand values. Keep existing small multi-placeholder behavior.
acceptance_tests: A permitted source template with many repeated placeholders and a large event must fail before allocating an oversized final payload or contacting a backend. Verify exact-limit success, over-limit refusal, UTF8 accounting and nested array/object expansion. Keep small repeated/missing-placeholder substitutions unchanged.
p4_findings.classification: Low-priority robustness of an optional operator-authored configuration; no claim of a normal-use production outage or live backend test.

held_candidate_dispositions.candidate: Backend once hooks consume their slot when no peer/provider effect starts
held_candidate_dispositions.reason: The backend handler itself was invoked and may intentionally count as the one attempt, consistent with HTTP failures consuming once. OS-child-specific started wording does not establish a clear incompatible user contract for in-process handlers. A change needs a product decision, so avoid manufacturing a defect.

No concrete consequential failure or project-specific limit contract established beyond general resource-hardening. The separate proven ignored-ancestor bug is already reported as P2; no duplicate issue.

Export renderer/import projections and hook backend once/async/MCP/model request behavior
